blocks.text: The English reflexive pronouns "myself", "yourself", etc. are rendered in Russian by the pronoun "**себя**", which is the same for all the genders, persons and numbers. "**Себя**" has no nominative case, since it can never be the subject of a sentence. In oblique cases it is declined like the pronoun "**ты**": **себя**, **себе**, **себя**, **собой**, **о себе**.

items: Я взял эту книгу для себя.
I took this book for myself.
Она посмотрела на себя в зеркало.
She looked at herself in the mirror.
The teacher took the map with him.

blocks.text: The idiomatic forms "**у себя**" and "**к себе**" are commonly used in the meaning of "at (or to) one's place": *Командир у себя в кабинете. Я иду к себе в комнату.* The verb "**чувствовать**" is used together with the accusative form "**себя**" in describing one's state of being: *Как вы чувствуете себя? — Я чувствую себя хорошо.*
From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 64.
